sanskrit: शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च । ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम् ॥
hindiTranslation: मनका निग्रह करना इन्द्रियोंको वशमें करना धर्मपालनके लिये कष्ट सहना बाहरभीतरसे शुद्ध रहना दूसरोंके अपराधको क्षमा करना शरीर, मन आदिमें सरलता रखना वेद, शास्त्र आदिका ज्ञान होना यज्ञविधिको अनुभवमें लाना और परमात्मा, वेद आदिमें आस्तिक भाव रखना  ये सबकेसब ब्राह्मणके स्वाभाविक कर्म हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Self-restraint, control of the senses, austerity, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, realization, and faith in the supreme reality are the natural duties of a brahmin.
essence: True duty begins as disciplined character, not public role.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: A person's natural work can include self-control, purity, forgiveness, honesty, knowledge, and trust in the supreme reality. These qualities belong to a brahmin by nature.
simpleInsight: Character is not random; it is trained through steady restraint, honesty, and inner cleanliness.
detailedMeaning: Krishna explains how human nature divides different kinds of work. After describing the qualities of brahmin life, he lists the inner disciplines that define it: calmness, self-control, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, knowledge, realization, and faith.
modernRelevance: A village schoolteacher keeps his temper with a rude parent and tells the truth about a child's marks. Those are the qualities Krishna lists for a brahmin: restraint, patience, honesty and learning lived out in ordinary work.
translationLiteral: शमः (control of the mind) / दमः (control of the senses) / तपः (austerity) / शौचम् (purity) / क्षान्तिः (forgiveness) / आर्जवम् (straightforwardness) / एव (indeed) / च (and) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / विज्ञानम् (realized understanding) / आस्तिक्यम् (faith) / ब्रह्मकर्म (brahmin duty) / स्वभावजम् (born of nature)
insight: Calm, restraint, austerity, purity, patience, honesty, knowledge, realization and faith: Krishna's list of a brahmin's natural duties.
